title: Chevrolet Nova Engines by Year (1962–1988)
description: Every factory engine in the Chevy II and Nova by year, 1962–1988: the 153 four and sixes, the 283 and 327, the L79, SS 350 and 396, and the Toyota-built 1.6.
intro: Chevrolet sold its compact as the Chevy II from 1962 and as the Nova from 1969, when the trim name became the model name, through 1979. The name returned for 1985–1988 on a front-drive car built with Toyota.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.

generations.name: Chevy II
intro: The first Chevy II offered a four and a six. Chevrolet added V8s in 1964, and the 327 followed in 1965, reaching 350 hp in the 1966 L79.

The 1968 redesign made room for the 396 big block, offered in the Nova SS through 1970, when it displaced 402 cubic inches. Ratings are SAE net from 1972, and the last Novas offered the 250 six, the 305 and the 350.
The front-drive Nova was built in California by NUMMI, a GM–Toyota joint venture, with Toyota's 1.6 four. The 1988 Twin Cam used a 16-valve version.

excluded.name: 283 V8
excluded.researchNote: NHRA and Chevy Hardcore list it for 1964, but the GM 1964 kit power-team chart (p.18) and ratings pages show only the 195-hp L32 283, and the GM-kit history reprint says the 4-bbl dual-exhaust 220-hp 283 was added to the Nova option list mid-year 1965. NovaResource shows it from 1965 only. Most likely not a 1964 factory option.

excluded.name: 327 V8
excluded.researchNote: Only NovaResource lists it. Not in the GM 1967 kit power teams or ratings; Chevy Hardcore says the L79 was not an official 1967 Chevy II offering (rumoured handful built). NHRA does not list it. Treat as not a catalogued 1967 option.

excluded.name: 427 V8
excluded.researchNote: Dealer conversion; not a factory Nova engine (Chevy Hardcore: 427s could not be factory-installed in the Nova).

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
